title: Air is all around us
keyIdea: Air is all around us, even though we cannot see it. We can feel it when it moves, and moving air can push light things: a fan pushes a feather, and the wind pushes leaves, kites and washing. A bag that looks empty is full of air, and a bubble has air inside. Air takes up space: push an upside-down cup into water and the air inside keeps the paper dry. Wind is air on the move; the trees do not make it.

kid: Air is all around you. You cannot see it. But you can feel it. Wave your hand by your face. That is air!
Moving air can push. Wave a fan and a feather flies. The wind is air on the move. It pushes leaves and kites.
A bag can look empty. But it is full of air. Squeeze it shut and it pushes back. A bubble has air in it too.
Push a cup down in water, upside down. The air in the cup keeps the water out. Tip it, and the air comes out in bubbles.
adult: In England this sits in the EYFS area Understanding the World. Development Matters (2021) asks 3 and 4 year olds to explore and talk about different forces they can feel, and the early learning goal The Natural World asks children to explore the world around them and talk about what they notice. In the US, the Head Start Early Learning Outcomes Framework puts it under Scientific Reasoning: observe and describe objects and events.

Air is a real thing even when it is still. It is a mix of gases, mostly nitrogen and oxygen. It has no colour, but it fills spaces and pushes on things. Wind is air moving from one place to another. A fan or a breath makes air move too. Light things move easily; heavy things like a rock do not move in a gentle wind.

Common mistakes to watch for: young children often say a bag or cup is empty when it is full of air; many think air is only there when it moves; and many say the trees make the wind by waving, which Piaget recorded in the 1920s and teachers still hear. Name air out loud, let them feel it push, and ask what moved the leaf.

In the lab your child waves a fan to push a feather into a box, catches air in a bag and squeezes it, blows and pops bubbles, finds what the wind moves outside, and pushes an upside-down cup into water so the paper inside stays dry. Every step works with big buttons or by tapping the picture. Read the Challenge aloud together.

familyTip: Tuck a dry tissue into the bottom of a cup. Turn it upside down and push it straight down into a bowl of water. Lift it out and feel the tissue: dry. Then try it tipped. On a windy day, look for 3 things the wind moves.

visual.caption: Can a puff of air move it? Drag each one, or tap it and then tap a box.

bins: A puff of air moves it

lab.caption: Flagship lab: wave a fan to push a feather, catch air in a bag, pop bubbles, find what the wind moves and keep paper dry in a cup under water.

choices: No, but we can feel it
No, so it is not there
practice.hint: Wave a hand by your face. What do you feel?
practice.explain: We cannot see air, but we can feel it move. It is all around us.

practice.prompt: You wave the fan {n} times. Each wave pushes the feather 1 step. How many steps does it go?
practice.explain: {n} waves push the feather {n} steps. Each wave moves the air.

practice.prompt: You blow {a} bubbles. Then you blow {b} more. How many bubbles of air?
practice.hint: Start at {a} and count on {b} more.
practice.explain: {a} and {b} more make {=a+b} bubbles. Each one has air inside.

practice.hint: What pushes the trees and makes them wave?
practice.explain: Wind is air on the move. It pushes the trees, so they wave.

pool.prompt: A bag is blown up and shut tight. What is inside?
pool.hint: Squeeze it. Does it push back?
pool.explain: It is full of air. That is why it pushes back when you squeeze.

pool.prompt: Which one can a puff of air move?
pool.hint: Is it light, or is it very heavy to lift?
pool.explain: A feather is light, so a puff of air moves it. A rock and a house are too heavy.

pool.prompt: You push a cup upside down into water. Is the tissue inside wet?
pool.hint: What is in the cup before the water?
pool.explain: Air fills the cup, so the water cannot get in. The tissue stays dry.

choices: Wave a hand by your face
pool.hint: Air has no colour. Can you feel it move?
pool.explain: Waving moves the air, and you feel it on your face.

pool.prompt: The wind moves {n} leaves. {k} leaves stay still under a rock. How many leaves in all?
pool.hint: Count the moving leaves, then count on the still ones.

pool.prompt: You tip the cup in the water. What comes up?
pool.hint: What was inside the cup before you tipped it?
pool.explain: The air comes out in bubbles, and the water goes in.

pool.prompt: You pop {p} of your {b} bubbles. How many bubbles are left?
pool.hint: Start at {b} and take away the {p} you popped.

pool.prompt: Is air still there when it is not windy?
choices: Yes, air is all around us
pool.hint: Wave your hand. Can you still feel air?
pool.explain: Yes. Air is all around us all the time. Wind is just air on the move.

pool.prompt: What pushes the kite up in the sky?
pool.hint: What moves outside on a windy day?
pool.explain: The wind, moving air, pushes the kite. The string holds it.
